subject: Guest join auth failure — manual provision / temp Zoom fallback
messages:
From: Kayla Ortiz <kayla@globridge.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: Globridge Tech Ops <techops@globridge.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo today — guests can’t join (Meet link)

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for setting up the 10:30 demo. We ran into a problem when two of our contractors tried to join — they get a permissions error that says they need "organization approval" to join the Google Meet. They are external to Globridge but can join other Meets fine.

We tried removing and reinviting them and they still see the blocked screen. The calendar invite is a Google Meet link (created by our calendar owner). Is there any way to issue a short-lived Zoom invite instead or give them temporary host rights? We're on a tight timeline — can the demo run in 45 minutes if we fix this?

Attaching a quick screenshot.

— Kayla

Attachments: meet-blocked-screen.png

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Kayla Ortiz <kayla@globridge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T09:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo today — guests can’t join (Meet link)

Kayla — sorry for the hiccup. Two quick options:

1) I can spin up a temporary Zoom link and post it to the thread in 10 minutes (we’ll be host so guests should be able to join).
2) If you prefer to keep Meet, we can provision a manual host token for one of your contractor emails so Google treats them as allowed — that takes ~15–20 minutes and requires your IT to accept a trust prompt.

Which do you prefer? If Zoom, I’ll create the meeting and send the new ICS. If Meet + token, please confirm the contractor emails and CC your techops contact so we can coordinate the prompt.

— Logan

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Kayla Ortiz <kayla@globridge.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T09:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo today — guests can’t join (Meet link)

Logan — if you do Zoom, make it a meeting (not webinar) and enable auto-admit for authenticated and non-authenticated users. Also, flag for recording (customer asked for a clip).

Kayla — quick note: if your org has Meet policy that blocks external guests unless the organizer is internal to your directory, Zoom is the faster path. We can handle recording and upload the clip to your Drive after the call.

— Ben

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Kayla Ortiz <kayla@globridge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T09:40:00-07:00

From: Kayla Ortiz <kayla@globridge.com>

Cc: Globridge Tech Ops <techops@globridge.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T09:52:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo today — guest join auth failure — (temporary zoom link)

Perfect — Zoom worked immediately for everyone. Thanks for the quick turnaround, Logan. Contractors joined and we were able to start on time. Recording would be great.

One follow-up request from our security team: they’d like a short note documenting why the Meet invite failed (policy vs organizer ownership) so we can file it internally. Can someone from Redwood provide a 2–3 line explanation we can attach to our incident log?

— Kayla

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Kayla Ortiz <kayla@globridge.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo today — guest join auth failure — follow-up note

Kayla — thanks again for the heads up. Short explanation for your security log:

"Issue: External guests were blocked from joining the Google Meet because the calendar organizer was tied to a domain policy that restricts guest admission unless explicitly allowed by the domain admin. Impact: prevented external attendees from joining the scheduled Meet. Workaround: Redwood created a temporary Zoom meeting and admitted guests manually to preserve the demo schedule. Recommended next step: have Globridge IT review calendar sharing settings or invite from an organizer within your domain to avoid Meet enforcement."

If you want this on company letterhead or with our CSM signature, we can produce a short PDF.

— Marissa (Customer Success)

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T16:00:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: retrospective and automation ask

Quick internal note for follow-up: root cause was calendar-organizer domain policy blocking external moderators. Action items:
- Create a quick KB for Sales to suggest Zoom fallback when Meet policies are unknown.
- Add an optional metadata flag on our demo invites (calendar:event -> invites:preferred_link) so we proactively include Zoom token for external-heavy accounts.

Ben — can you add the KB draft to the sales playbook? Marissa — I’ll loop CSM for a PDF if Globridge asks.

— Logan
